newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to check whether it erred in phone tender. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israel to check whether it erred in phone tender. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]

text.p: The Israeli Communications Ministry tenders committee will meet on Sunday to decide whether it erred in how it awarded two international telephone service licences, the ministry's spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"The decision to convene the committee follows the appeal in Tel Aviv District Court on the results of the tender," she said.
Communications Minister Limor Livnat would not comment.

The Dolphin group earlier this week won a temporary order barring the ministry from awarding the two licences. Dolphin claimed that the scoring of the six bids competing in the government tender to award the licences was done incorrectly.

Dolphin comprises Bellsouth Corp, the Safra family, Israel's Disount Investment Corp, Israsat and Canada's Teleglobe, (corrects from "Dolphin comprises MCI, British Telecom, Israel's Tadiran Ltd and two Israeli companies").
One of the two groups that won the tender, announced in early November, was Golden Lines, which comprises SBC Communications, Italy's STET and three Israeli partners.
The second was Barak, which includes Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and two Israeli companies -- Clalcom Ltd and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
Although the ministry did not say which of the two licences might be in jeopardy, in announcing the results of the tender early last month it said Barak had come in second in the scoring.
The tender entitles the licencees to offer overseas telephone service in competition with state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecom.
